dead_reckoning.description: Inertial integration with no aiding at all. Reported as the control for "how much of the result is the filter and how much is the motion model".
dead_reckoning.name: dead_reckoning

gnss_only.description: GNSS at 5 Hz, no outage, no vision. This is the reference point every other case is read against; it establishes that the filter is calibrated when a satellite solution is available.
gnss_only.name: gnss_only

outage_control.description: 15 s GNSS outage, 5 s to 20 s, with vision OFF. This is the honest baseline for a contested receiver: the error grows, the filter knows it grows, and the coverage stays at nominal throughout.
outage_control.name: outage_control

scenario.description: GNSS outage with no visual aiding.
scenario.name: outage_control

outage_visual.description: The same 15 s outage with vision ON. This is the case the 21-state refactor was supposed to fix, and the numbers say it did not: the filter reports roughly 0.3 m of uncertainty while being tens of metres wrong, and coverage collapses. That is why vision_enabled defaults to false, and why closing the gap needs a pose graph rather than a better filter.
outage_visual.name: outage_visual

scenario.description: GNSS outage with visual aiding, 21-state anchor.
scenario.name: outage_visual

outage_visual_degraded_camera.description: Visual aiding through the outage with 30% of camera frames dropped in bursts. Checks that the anchor model does not collapse when the visual stream is intermittent rather than clean.
outage_visual_degraded_camera.name: outage_visual_degraded_camera

vision_anchor_in_measurement_noise.description: The pre-refactor arrangement, where the visual anchor error is folded into the measurement covariance. Retained as a regression control, not as a supported configuration.
vision_anchor_in_measurement_noise.name: vision_anchor_in_measurement_noise

scenario.description: Anchor error in R rather than in filter state (incorrect).
scenario.name: vision_anchor_in_measurement_noise

vision_only.description: Visual odometry at 20 Hz with no GNSS. Calibrated, and much better than dead reckoning, but it cannot be trusted for an unbounded outage: a single anchor held for a long run freezes the position uncertainty.
vision_only.name: vision_only

disclaimer: All numbers are from a known-answer synthetic fixture. They are not field measurements and must not be presented as real-sensor performance.
